main_text.head: CAP. III. Complectens exemplum Caini & Jacobi Patriarchæ.
main_text.p: Sub lege naturæ tum sacerdotii jus, tum principatus primogenituræ fuisse annexa notius est, quàm ut à me ulteriori aliqua explicatione indigeat, unica illa Jacobi Patriarchæ sufficiat vox, {e}Ruben primogenitus meus, tua fortitudo mea, & principium roboris mei, prior in donis, major in imperio: in donis proir [?] ad obeundum munus sacerdotii, & in imperio maior ad officium principatus subeundum: Jam verò Cain fuisse Adami primogenitum, vel ex ipso nomine apparet. Gen.29.3

Quamprimùm enim eum peperisset, dixit Evah, {f}Possedi hominem per Deum, quod utique non dixisset, si alios filios ante Cain genuisset; in illos enim potiùs quàm in Cain, id nominis conveniebat. Gen. 4.1.
Non igitur mirandum, cùm in persona Cain honor principatus inhæserit, licèt fratrem suum crudeliter interfecerit, procaciter Deo responderit,

page.notes: The first letter "S" of the opening paragraph is a large woodcut-style initial, read as "S" + "ub" and normalised to "Sub". The word "proir" is printed as seen and marked [?]; it may be a misprint for "prior". The word "Adami" is preceded by a printed sign over the A, which is not transcribed. The marginal notes are "e Gen.29.3" and "f Gen. 4.1.", keyed to the superscript marks e and f in the text. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
